verdicts.note: Tested toward +2 and toward 0. He has never held elected office and offers 'a fresh set of eyes' against a three-term sheriff [S1], so the score leans toward new voices. But he spent 27 years in law enforcement, seven of them in this same sheriff's office [S1], so +1 at medium is right, not +2. This matches the Adams sheriff challenger.

The direction holds. His one operational priority is 'an aggressive approach towards theft and drug abuse' to keep people secure in their homes and on their property [S1]. That points to enforcement, and he states no diversion or treatment agenda. The magnitude does not hold. This is a single sentence with no program behind it: no staffing plan, no stance on repeat offenders, no named enforcement tactic. 'Drug abuse' targets use, not trafficking, and an aggressive approach to it could include treatment. The same statement promises to lead with 'compassion' [S1]. One rhetorical sentence from a pamphlet-only candidate supports -1, not the maximal -2. That also puts him level with Maycumber's -1, which is fair given that the contest dossier calls both candidates enforcement-oriented.

Tested toward -1 and it does not hold. He has been sheriff since January 2015, is finishing a third term, and has held Ferry County law-enforcement posts since 2001, all of which his statement puts forward [S1]. That is the maximal proven-record profile, and high confidence fits a fact drawn from his own statement. Trailing in the primary [S3] does not change how he frames the race.

Tested toward 0. He describes hiring and retention as a problem that comes from the county's 'inability to allocate funding to attract applicants' [S1]. He does not lay out an agenda. Still, police staffing is the named pole_a item, and nothing in the dossier points toward prevention, diversion or non-police response. The rest of his statement covers his tenure's challenges and his SSSB 5974 lawsuit, which is recorded but not scored [S1][S2]. -1 at medium fits, consistent with the Adams sheriff incumbent. The funding complaint could look like a spending (invest) signal, but it describes a shortfall and makes no proposal, so no spending score is warranted.
